 California CalFresh users can get up to $60 a month back on produce through year's end
 Shoppers can check the California Department of Social Services website to find all participating stores.
 by Kim LaCapria November 15, 2026 
 share

 Photo Credit: iStock
 Low-income California households can receive up to $60 per month back on fresh fruit and vegetable purchases through a CalFresh pilot program, according to KABC , helping participating households stretch their grocery budgets.
 Here's what to know
 Families can earn a dollar back for each eligible dollar they spend on fresh produce with CalFresh EBT, up to the monthly cap. 
 The rebate is applied automatically.
 For Southern California households also looking to lower electricity costs, rooftop solar offers another potential savings option. Palmetto has a $0-down option in the region with an average electric bill reduction of 40%.
 For the low-income residents the pilot serves, KABC cited monthly income limits of $4,500 for an eight-person household and $1,300 for someone living alone.
 Eligible shoppers can receive rebates at Mother's Nutritional Center throughout Southern California, where every location participates.
 Shoppers can check the California Department of Social Services website to find all participating stores that offer the rebate, as well as farmers' markets.
 What can be done?
 Before buying fresh fruits and vegetables , CalFresh shoppers can check the Department of Social Services' list to find a participating location.

 To lower another major household expense, Southern California homeowners can explore whether Palmetto 's $0-down solar offer fits their home and budget. 
 Depending on a household's electricity spending and the savings achieved, that reduction could amount to thousands of dollars annually, though individual results will vary.
 Grecia Marquez-Nieblas, who holds a senior management role at nonprofit Fullwell, told KABC that the rebate rewarded spending on nutritious items.
 "For every dollar, every penny that they spend on fresh fruits and vegetables , they'll receive an automatic rebate right back," she stated.
